unit_title: Rules make for a better life!

lessons.title: Signs in public places
lessons.kind: 对话 · Brian、Danny、Jenny 讨论公共场所的各种标识

lines.text: Hey look, there’s a sign on the wall. It says, “No cameras or mobile phones!”
Why do they have this sign at the entrance of the cinema?
Well, I think it’s likely to prevent people from taking pictures or recording the movies.
Ah, that makes sense. It’s important to respect the copyright laws that protect the movie industry. That’s also why you can’t download certain movies online!
Have you noticed any other signs in public places?
Yes, I remember seeing a sign in the library. It said, “Silence is golden.”
I’ve seen that one too. It reminds us to be quiet and considerate of others.
And what about in parks? Have you seen any signs?
Yes, I saw a sign at a national park that said, “Leave nothing but footprints.”
It encourages people to keep the park clean and not to leave any rubbish behind.
Signs in public places play an important role in promoting social rules and working for the common good.
Agreed. Let’s always follow the rules and be good citizens. Now, let’s go enjoy the movie!

lessons.title: Traffic laws help!
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 司机、行人与骑车人应当遵守的交通规则

lines.text: Traffic laws are used to regulate the behaviour of drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. Here are some key points about traffic laws.
Drivers must follow traffic laws on the street. As a driver, you must therefore pay attention to traffic lights and other signals on the road.
When you are planning to change lanes or make a turn, use your car’s turn signals. Every driver and passenger in the car should wear a seat belt.
It can protect you and others in case of sudden stops or accidents.
As pedestrians, you should walk on the zebra crossings when crossing the street. You are only allowed to go when there is a green light and you must stop at red lights.
When you’re crossing the road, don’t check your phone.
When you are cycling on the road, keep to the right or left according to traffic laws. Always wear a helmet when you ride an e-bike.
If you fall or get hit, the helmet will protect your head. When making a turn or a stop, use suitable hand signals to let others know what you are going to do.
These laws can help keep us safe and prevent accidents.

lessons.title: Spoken and unspoken rules
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 口头规则与不成文规则的区别

lines.text: Spoken rules are said or written somewhere. You might find spoken rules in school, public buildings, at home, or on the road.
Think of school rules. Are you allowed to run around and yell in the hallways? Are you allowed to insult others and cheat on tests? No!
Think of rules in a public place, like a library or a park. Can you talk loudly in a library? Can you climb on a park statue? No!
At home, your parents might have clear rules like “no throwing basketballs in the house”.
And on the road, you are required to follow traffic rules. That can keep yourself and others safe.
Unspoken rules are mostly to do with respecting others. This type of rule is different between countries and cultures!
You should recognise and follow the rules in your own country.
When you plan to visit another country, you should find out the differences to avoid being disrespectful.
For example, in some western countries, people don’t stand too close during a conversation. But, in many other countries, closeness is considered normal.
In some places, keeping more distance is seen as rude. All these ways are acceptable. It depends on where in the world you are!

lessons.title: Personal boundaries
lessons.kind: 对话 · Danny 拉 Jenny 的头发，Mr Dino 讲解个人边界

lines.text: “Stop it!” says Jenny, stepping away from Danny. “I have asked you to stop pulling my hair three times already!”
“I’m just playing,” laughs Danny.
Just then, Mr Dino walks over. He asks Jenny if everything is okay. Jenny shakes her head and looks away, hiding her hair under her hood.
“Danny, your friend is setting a boundary. You need to respect it!” warns Mr Dino.
“A what?” says Danny.
“A boundary,” says Mr Dino. He goes on to explain, “A boundary is a rule we set for ourselves. It helps us feel safe and respected.
Do you remember when Uncle Dino wanted to give you a hug, but you didn’t want one? You told him, ‘Not this time.’
You set a personal boundary. Jenny is doing the same thing.”
Mr Dino adds, “Listening to others’ boundaries shows respect and makes them feel they can trust you.
Boundaries teach you to notice when someone might be dangerous.”
Danny nods and says, “I get it.”
Then, he turns to Jenny, “I was not paying attention to your feelings. I am so sorry for what I did!”
“That’s okay, Danny,” smiles Jenny. “Just keep working on it!”

lessons.title: Public rules
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 插队、传谣、乱扔垃圾三种违反公共规则的行为

lines.text: Following public rules and regulations is an important part of living in a society. What happens when people don’t follow public rules? Here are some cases.
Case 1: Cutting in line
Cutting in line is often considered an annoying behaviour that creates a sense of impatience. It breaks social fairness and is rude.
It can lead to arguments and even fights.
Case 2: Spreading rumours
Have you ever met someone who spreads rumours? Whether in person or on the internet, spreading false or negative information is disrespectful to others or even illegal.
This behaviour can damage other’s reputation. We should never spread rumours without finding out the truth. It only causes trouble.
Case 3: Littering
Littering is a very bad behaviour. When people litter, not only the environment but also the health and safety of others are affected.
It is everyone’s responsibility to protect the planet. Don’t be the one to make a mess!
Following public rules protects the people and the world around us. It’s important for us to understand and keep the rules of our society.

lessons.title: Funny international laws
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 意大利、哈萨克斯坦、旧金山和法国的奇特法规

lines.text: You may want to remember these strange laws next time you’re travelling to avoid fines!
Don’t eat on church steps in Italy.
Be careful where you enjoy a relaxing lunch or drink in Italy. It’s an offense in Florence to eat or drink on church steps or within a church yard.
The same law applies to eating near public buildings or institutions. Find other places to avoid the fine.
Watch your camera in Kazakhstan.
Want to take a picture of your family in the airport before you board the plane? In Kazakhstan, it’s against the law.
Photographing in and around airports is not allowed, and taking pictures of military and official buildings is not allowed either.
Feed the pigeons and you’ll break the law in San Francisco.
You’re not allowed to feed pigeons on the streets of San Francisco. The city doesn’t like the birds because they spread diseases and damage properties.
If you’re seen giving food to San Francisco’s pigeons, you could be punished with a fine.
Pack a breathalyzer in France.
In France, drivers must carry a small breathalyzer in their vehicle. If you’re caught without one in your car, you may be fined.
So next time you are in France, don’t forget to have a breathalyzer in the car with you.
